requirements.text: A reservation is not residency, and one predicate answers both the gate and the report. Tier tokens are taken at CLAIM and only bound occupancy. A movement node is RESIDENT only when it still holds its tier tokens AND a current map fragment for this consumer/tier/manifest vouches for the bytes (plan stage root on the stage leg; announced ram root under the announced epoch on the ram leg) AND it is not claimed/ AND a complete record_move receipt covers the plan-sealed span AND that receipt's entries_declared == entries_staged equals the current fragment's entry count. No payload read, no hashing, no whole-manifest stat. Unreadable or malformed evidence is UNKNOWN and is never reported as not-staged; the census reports the booking as reserved beside staged. UNKNOWN survives aggregation: cursor_gap counts unstaged_phases/unstaged_bytes only for a false leg, carries unknown_phases/unknown_bytes beside them additively against remaining_phases, and a chunked leg is true only when every chunk is, false as soon as one chunk is known missing, unknown otherwise. Testing a three-state answer with 'is not True' is banned. prismabuild_residency_unstaged_* therefore counts known backlog only.

PB publishes no successor until the predecessor's retirement commits.

requirements.target_enforcement: contract prose plus review; no new sealing work authorized
requirements.text: Producer commit boundaries and recovery requirements are unchanged; this row adds a persistence-assumption requirement and does not weaken them. Atomic rename places a record, and verified publication evidence (the published record read back and validated) establishes that it is present and re-readable. A rename, fsync, digest, or CAS receipt does not prove stronger persistence, and none proves power-loss durability when the backing dataset's sync policy is asynchronous or disabled. When stable-storage durability is required, sync=disabled does not satisfy it. State the persistence assumption wherever a claim depends on it. Observed for this campaign: storage_pool/shared has sync=disabled, so receipts, digests, and recovery on volatile writes confer no physical durability; an earlier reading of the parent storage_pool dataset as sync=standard was wrong and retracted. No durability sealing work and no automatic dataset policy change is authorized.
